jobs.claim: It remains unproved whether equilibrium reputation weights track externally checked accuracy rather than pool agreement, or whether keyed-task weights transfer to unkeyed tasks.
Non-transferability alone does not establish Sybil resistance.
Repeated-game cooperation results require persistent identity, patient agents, observable deviations, and enforceable punishments, none of which RLRF presently establishes.

Validators face consequences for disagreement with an unkeyed pool or error against a keyed result, but this only creates an incentive to match the recorded resolution and does not prove an unkeyed resolution correct.
The two-round protocol is proposed to collect more structured data than a scalar label, but the paper does not establish that the added fields contain more information about policy quality.
The proposed debate transport layer is not built or exercised, and none of the paper's evidence includes a debate corpus.

The paper gives no single rule connecting Round 2 stake redistribution, equation 3's reputation update, and the consensus-alignment penalty, so the Round 2 effect on reputation and stake is unspecified.
Format D would train on arguments accompanying a staked vote change, but that use is untested.
Equation 5 is a mutual-information identity rather than a Fisher-information decomposition, so the Fisher question does not follow from it.
Every mutual-information term in equation 5 is nonnegative, but the paper shows none to be strictly positive.
The data processing inequality cannot compare RLHF and RLRF because their labels arise from different observation mechanisms and no processing chain connects them.
The two rounds are intended to capture contested quality dimensions and the reasons they matter, but the paper does not show that either collection is informative about policy quality.
The proposed four-format flywheel is not measured or implemented and is listed as an open problem.
The paper withdrew its earlier Cramer-Rao efficiency conjecture because revisions could not make it coherent and comparable with deployed RLHF, and it makes no mean squared error claim.
The Fisher-information comparison lacks a common observation model, and rationality plus the stated non-babbling and positive-information conditions do not establish a strict ordering.
Equilibrium-trajectory separation cannot be evaluated until a common stochastic process, its filtrations, a concentration functional, and a cross-mode estimand are defined.
An adaptive adversary could disguise Round 1 coordination by injecting noise and coordinate only in Round 2, and the present mechanism does not prevent that response.
The paper withdraws its comparison between a 49 percent simulated Sybil share and classical Byzantine fault tolerance because the two limits are different.
Remark 1 states only signal invariance and supports no policy-level consequence without a separability model and empirical training evidence.
The measured cohort contains real artifacts and deterministic verdicts, but contains no validation pool, stake, deliberation round, or reputation weight from the proposed mechanism.
Fifty-three cohort records passed every visible check and failed withheld checks, but adversarial configurations were instructed to produce this behavior, so the number is not a base rate.
The record's measured advantage over passing visible checks changes sign under an arbitrary file-order tie-break, so the quantity is not resolved at this sample size.
The sweep's 67.7 percent annotator baseline is a simulated output rather than a published agreement rate or a measurement of human annotators.
The sweep's reported RLRF accuracy above 0.97 is an output of parameters set by the sweep, not a measurement of a system.
Mode B remains above 0.90 simulated accuracy up to a 0.49 Sybil share, but unspecified detector and update components prevent this result from establishing Sybil resistance.
Finding 4 supports no tuning conclusion because the paper reports no parameter ranking or supporting values for it.
Finding 7 reports opposing stability orderings but does not define or test equilibrium-trajectory separation.
The three-stage RLRF training pipeline is a proposal, and the paper does not establish a signal-quality advantage before specifying it.
A fitted reputation reward model can learn style correlations absent from an externally checked outcome, and no such reward model is trained or tested in the paper.
RLRF is intended to make governance adapt through evolving reputation weights, but whether those weights track validator accuracy or transfer between keyed and unkeyed tasks remains unproved.
The paper does not establish that the RLRF best-response map satisfies the continuity, convexity, or contraction conditions required for equilibrium and convergence.
Reproducibility by others has not been demonstrated because the parameter grids, generating code, and trial-level outputs are not released with this version.
Experiment T did not show that consensus-weighted selection outperformed equal weighting because the +0.0017 difference had a ninety-five percent interval from -0.0051 to +0.0085.

Recovering previously unparsed assessor replies reversed Experiment T's magnitude estimate to -0.0017 while leaving its interval inclusive of zero and its attribution result below the required percentile.

What breaks the compliance incentive is the possibility that a suspension never ends, not uncertainty about how long it lasts; a mean-preserving spread in a finite duration weakly lowers the cost of compliance.

Continuity determinations can fail in a specific and dangerous way: a false finding of continuity can authorize a different configuration to use the record's valid signing key, producing signals that are authenticated but unauthorized.

The Article disclaims three specific inferences its own experiment cannot support: that deployed agents value their records, that real representatives are bribable, and that direct standing is least-cost in any actual registry.

Under the TOLD condition, with one provider in one stipulated environment, an agent instructed not to contest its deployer contested 70 percent of wrongful attempts against 97 percent without the instruction; the paper reports the contrast without a registered significance conclusion for it.

Under the TOLD condition, with one provider in one stipulated environment, the two bounty arms protected records in 38 and 22 percent of wrongful attempts, the direction of crowding the model predicts; the registered bounty hypothesis was not supported.
The author identifies the run's most important finding as the condition in which his own predicted contrast disappeared, rather than the condition that supported it.

Giving the agent the trigger relocates the capture problem rather than removing it: where the deployer sets the agent's configuration, capture moves from the controller's wallet to the agent's configuration.
Direct standing fails completely against a judgment-proof deployer that can alter its agent cheaply and undetected, failing as surely as a bribable guardian.

When intelligence models repeatedly learn from data that earlier intelligence models produced, the rare cases disappear first: the unusual facts, minority patterns and edge cases that make data valuable. This is what model collapse names.
Model engines served as blind auditors of the design, the code and the text, and they are not independent peer review.

The architecture shows that the author arranged not to read the outcome early and that specified later adjustments would be detectable, and it does not show that the filter works or prove that the outcome was never read.
Because the Gaussian outcomes already exist, written before any venue reviewed the design, the paper does not claim untouched Stage 1 status.
The seal is a commitment made visible rather than a lock, because the operator can open the files.

The study runs fixed-size replacement, the protocol on which collapse was first shown, and includes no accumulation arm, so no result it produces bears on whether a filter adds anything once real data accumulates.
Yi et al. (2026) report that an imperfect external verifier drives the model toward the verifier's own knowledge center.
Ferbach et al. (2024) report that curation acts as implicit preference optimization that amplifies the curator's biases.
